decisions.reason: Product A builds closely on the firm's existing fluid-handling and fabricated metal capabilities, so the firm can interpret and improve it, indicating a low probability of being dropped.
Product B is distant from the firm's established offer and the firm lacks related knowledge to assimilate and improve it, so it is likely to be dropped.
Product C builds on the firm's established metal component skills, allowing the firm to learn from early results and apply improvements, so it is likely to be kept.
Product D builds on the firm's established offer but uses cast iron rather than steel/stainless, giving the firm somewhat less absorptive capacity, though still related enough to keep.
Product E builds directly on the firm's steel processing expertise, so absorptive capacity is high and it is likely to be kept.
